[[https://github.com/ryjm/ogent/actions/workflows/ci.yml][https://github.com/ryjm/ogent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg]]

*Use LLMs in structured Org workflows*

ogent brings language models into Org-mode the Emacs way: composable commands with text + org-mode as the universal interface.

** Exoskeleton + Agent

ogent is designed around this constraint:

- *Make review fast*: Responses land in Org blocks you can fold, diff, and navigate with standard keybindings. Tree based navigation beats scrolling and =C-c C-c= beats ad-hoc copy pasting for context management.

- *Make context explicit*: You declare what goes in via =@handles=, pins, and codemap. Obviously just giving it the whole project works too.

** Features

- *Context as data*: =@handles= resolve to Org nodes, files, or org-roam entries. Codemap indexes your project. Pins persist across requests.

- *Responses as structure*: Output lands in src blocks with metadata (=:model=, =:status=, =:latency=). Fold them, edit them, version them. It's just Org.

- *Edits as diffs*: Code changes render as smerge conflicts. Accept with =C-c C-c=, reject with =C-c C-k=.

- *Commands*: =C-c . RET= runs the current bullet as the prompt, with parent bullets passed as =# Parent Bullets= context. =C-c . q= asks a new minibuffer question about the current subtree. =C-c . ?= shows the ask menu. =C-c . p= opens full dispatch. =C-c . E= requests code edits.

- *Armory*: A local agent workspace built from plain Org files. Armory gives you persistent agents, jobs, conversations, approvals, schedules, task boards, data views, git state, and generated app artifacts without leaving Emacs.

* Requirements
- Emacs 29.1 or newer
- Org 9.8.7 or newer
- [[https://github.com/karthink/gptel][gptel]] 0.9.9.5 or newer for transport and model selection
- [[https://github.com/magit/transient][transient]] 0.13.5 or newer for command menus
- Optional: [[https://www.orgroam.com/][org-roam]] for cross-file handle resolution
- An LLM provider:
  - **OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT**: Reuse Codex CLI OAuth credentials
  - **Claude Code / Claude Max/Pro**: Use OAuth authentication (recommended, no API key needed)
  - **API Key**: Traditional API key for Anthropic or OpenAI

* Install
1. Clone the repository:
   #+begin_src shell
   git clone https://github.com/ryjm/ogent.git
   cd ogent
   #+end_src
2. Ensure dependencies compile cleanly:
   #+begin_src shell
   make lint
   make test
   #+end_src
3. Add =lisp/= and =lisp/ui/= to your =load-path=, then require =ogent=:
   #+begin_src emacs-lisp
   (add-to-list 'load-path (expand-file-name "lisp" "/path/to/ogent"))
   (add-to-list 'load-path (expand-file-name "lisp/ui" "/path/to/ogent"))
   (require 'ogent)
   #+end_src

* Agent tools and local checks
Use familiar names, named arguments, and structured results after loading
ogent. These local SDK workflows need no provider login or inference:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(ogent-agent-describe "read" 'json) ; Exact arguments, aliases, examples, and approval policy
(let ((page (ogent-agent-call "read" '(:file_path "README.org" :limit 20))))
  (ogent-agent-next page))         ; Follow the exact position; reject changed snapshots
(ogent-agent-batch
 '[(:tool "files" :args (:pattern "**/*.el" :limit 5))
   (:tool "search" :args (:pattern "defun" :path "lisp" :limit 5))])
(ogent-agent-capabilities 'json)   ; All live tool contracts
(ogent-agent-schema 'json)         ; Version 1 result envelope schema
(ogent-agent-triage 'json)         ; Local health and next actions
#+end_src

Results separate =status=, =data=, =error=, and page continuations. Empty files
and no matches succeed. Async calls deliver one terminal result; read-only
batches validate the whole plan before running. Writes and shell commands
retain the existing approval, edit review, and ledger flow.

Discovery reads the current registry; =(ogent-tools-install-defaults)= explicitly
adds built-in specs when needed. Existing integrations keep text output by
default; =ogent-tools-result-format= can opt registered calls into =json=.
=make test format=json= and =make lint format=json= report actual
compiler/test results with diagnostics on stderr. See
[[file:docs/agent-ergonomics.org][the agent interface guide]] for pagination, async calls, bounds, and migration.

* Configuration
** Quick Setup (Recommended)
Run =M-x ogent-onboard= to interactively configure your LLM provider. This wizard:
1. Lets you choose between OpenAI Codex OAuth, Claude Code OAuth, or API key authentication
2. Guides you through the login process
3. Configures gptel backends automatically
4. Run =M-x ogent-doctor= at any time to check Emacs/package versions,
   gptel/backend state, br availability, and local OAuth caches without
   making network calls.

** OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT OAuth
If you already use the Codex CLI with ChatGPT login, ogent reads supported credentials (including OAuth tokens)
cached in =$CODEX_HOME/auth.json= or =~/.codex/auth.json=:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'ogent)
(ogent-codex-login)         ; Opens Codex browser login
(ogent-codex-login-device)  ; Device-code fallback for headless sessions
#+end_src

After login, choose =OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT (OAuth - Recommended)= in
=M-x ogent-onboard=.

To check status: =M-x ogent-codex-status=
To logout: =M-x ogent-codex-logout=

** Claude Code / Claude Max/Pro OAuth
If you have a Claude Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account, you can
authenticate via the Claude Code-compatible OAuth flow:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(require 'ogent)
(ogent-claude-code-login)  ; Opens browser, paste the code
#+end_src

This stores refresh tokens in =~/.emacs.d/ogent/anthropic-oauth/= and automatically
refreshes them as needed, so there is no API key to manage.

** Vanilla Emacs (API Key)
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-hook 'org-mode-hook #'ogent-mode)
(setq ogent-default-model "gpt-6.1-sol")
#+end_src

** Doom Emacs
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(package! ogent :recipe (:local-repo "/path/to/ogent/lisp" :files ("*.el" "ui/*.el")))
(use-package! ogent
  :after org
  :init
  (setq ogent-enable-doom-bindings t
        ogent-doom-prefix "o")
  :config
  (ogent-setup-doom-bindings)
  (ogent-global-mode 1))
#+end_src

* Usage
- Open any Org buffer and toggle =ogent-mode= (or rely on =ogent-global-mode=).
- Write a normal Org bullet/heading, then press =C-c . RET= to run that subtree as the prompt; ogent inserts a compact =Request:= / =Response= transcript below it.
- Parent bullets are sent explicitly under =# Parent Bullets= for Zen runs: each parent contributes its own body text, never its children, so nothing is duplicated and prior transcripts never leak into the payload.
- Workspace selection is prose-first: a bullet like =look in ~/vault/projects/ogent for ideas= makes that directory the request workspace. Explicit labels (=Context:=, =Workspace:=, =Project:=, =Repo:=) still work, but are optional. The payload shows a =# Workspace= section, relative ogent tool paths resolve from that root, and code-grounded wording asks gptel to use read-only tools before answering.
- Re-run a bullet from anywhere inside its transcript: =C-c . RET= appends a fresh run, =C-c . != (or =C-c C-c= on the transcript) replaces it. Earlier runs collapse automatically when a new run starts.
- Press =C-c . q= to ask a new minibuffer question about the subtree at point.
- Press =C-c . ?= when you are unsure: the ask menu names the active scope and offers run-current-bullet, re-run, inline ask, popup ask, malleable region ask/rewrite, edit application, context preview, and the full dispatcher.
- Press =C-c . p= to open the dispatcher, pick models, and send the current subtree.
- Doom/Evil users get the same command surface under =SPC o= when =ogent-setup-doom-bindings= or evil bindings are active.
- Use =C-c . c= for a context preview and =C-c . m= to inspect the codemap.
- Press =C-c . d= to capture the last AI response to a Notes child heading.
- To attach reusable prompt snippets, create Org nodes with an =OGENT_ID= (see =docs/prompts.org=).

** Zen notebook presentation
=ogent-zen-mode= (enabled with =ogent-mode= in Org buffers; see
=ogent-zen-enable-in-org=) keeps the page quiet without touching the
stored text.  To turn it on for every Org buffer independently of
=ogent-mode=, enable =global-ogent-zen-mode= (it activates in Org
buffers only and skips internal scratch buffers):
- Heading stars compose into a uniform bullet (=ogent-zen-bullet=,
  default =•=; skipped automatically when org-modern, org-bullets, or
  org-superstar is active).
- Generated =Request:= / =Response= headings render as compact run cards:
  expanded requests stay prompt-first, while folded completed requests
  become result-first indexes such as =✓ 10 grounded ideas · from “Better
  headline display”=.  Folded results can add a muted virtual preview line
  (=ogent-zen-folded-result-preview=) without changing the stored Org.
  Request metadata is split into outcome badges and lower-priority
  right-aligned metadata when the window can support it; density is
  customizable with =ogent-zen-result-headline-density= (=minimal=,
  =balanced=, =rich=, or =debug=).
  Multi-model runs show model chips, selected/accepted responses, and
  sibling lineage such as =latest= or =superseded by newer run=.  Active
  tool work is promoted into the main title (=reading lisp/ogent-zen.el ·
  Headline idea=) rather than buried in a suffix.  Tool-call failures stay
  as inline diagnostics instead of failing the run card; only request-level
  model/network/abort failures turn the headline red.  Empty runs show
  =0 chars= instead of a vague warning.
  Response headings are quieter secondary rows and, when folded, carry
  response-local result previews plus review badges.  Zen review now
  persists a structured decision model (=OGENT_DECISION=,
  =OGENT_REVIEW_STATUS=, =OGENT_USEFULNESS=, =OGENT_LINEAGE=,
  =OGENT_OUTCOME=, timestamps, reviewer, and a visible =:REVIEW:= drawer)
  while keeping legacy =OGENT_REVIEW= in sync for older transcripts.
  Review can explicitly target the run or one response, can accept a
  response as the selected model, and exposes a queue/dashboard workflow
  under =C-c ,=.  Active requests animate only in visible buffers
  (=ogent-zen-pretty-headings=).  Parent breadcrumb suffixes are opt-in
  via =ogent-zen-show-breadcrumbs=.  Overlay-local =RET= / =r= / =u= /
  =e= action hints and bindings are opt-in via =ogent-zen-heading-actions=
  so Evil and other modal keymaps keep owning those keys by default.
  Use =C-c . w= (=ogent-zen-copy-response=) anywhere in a Zen transcript
  to copy only the response body, without request metadata or headings.
  Malleable editing uses the same tree-context machinery at smaller scope:
  =C-c . C-r= (=ogent-zen-run-region=) asks about the active region,
  =C-c . C-e= (=ogent-zen-edit-dwim=) rewrites the active region /
  paragraph / sentence with a SEARCH/REPLACE response, and =C-c . C-a=
  (=ogent-zen-apply-last-edit=) replays the latest structured edit into
  an inline diff preview.  Accept or reject the preview with
  =ogent-zen-accept-edit= / =ogent-zen-reject-edit= (or
  =inline-diff-mode='s =C-c C-c= / =C-c C-k=).  Tool calls no longer
  inline into the notebook: Zen records them out of band so repeated
  prompt submissions stay responsive, keeps a compact count on the
  request headline, and opens the full list (arguments, results, status)
  in a separate buffer with =C-c . h= (=ogent-zen-show-tool-calls=).
  Set =ogent-zen-tool-calls-inline= to restore the legacy inline
  =:TOOL:= drawers.  Transcript property drawers and prompt blocks fold
  away immediately (=ogent-zen-fold-noise=), and earlier runs collapse
  with status, model, result titles, and =superseded= lineage when a new
  run starts (=ogent-zen-collapse-previous-runs=).
- Set =ogent-zen-center-column= to an integer (e.g. =80=) to center the
  notebook in wide windows.
Disabling the mode restores plain Org; the underlying transcript is
always standard =Request:= / =Response= text, so history replay and
older tooling keep working.

* Prompt Templates

ogent includes a library of reusable prompt templates for common workflows.
Templates are defined in =docs/prompts.org= and can be referenced using =@handle= syntax.

** Using Prompt Templates

Apply a template from the prompt dispatcher's Templates infix (=T= in
=M-x ogent-prompt-dispatch=), or with =M-x ogent-prompt-insert=, which inserts
the composed template text at point. With the optional yasnippet integration
(see below), type a template's handle and press =TAB= to expand it inline:

#+begin_example
@code-review
#+end_example

** Composing Multiple Templates

Select more than one template from the Templates infix or =ogent-prompt-insert=;
ogent concatenates them, ordered by each template's =compose-order=. The
=@handle+@handle= shorthand is accepted by the compose API
(=ogent-prompt-compose-from-string=):

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(ogent-prompt-compose-from-string "@code-review+@security-audit")
#+end_src

** Available Templates

| Template            | Purpose                                      |
|---------------------+----------------------------------------------|
| =@code-review=      | Review code for bugs, style, performance     |
| =@refactoring=      | Suggest refactoring opportunities            |
| =@documentation=    | Generate docstrings and comments             |
| =@testing=          | Suggest test cases and edge cases            |
| =@explain-code=     | Explain what code does step by step          |
| =@debug-steps=      | Systematic debugging approach                |
| =@security-audit=   | Audit for security vulnerabilities           |
| =@performance-review= | Review for performance issues              |

See =docs/prompts.org= for the full list and detailed instructions.

** Creating Custom Templates

Create Org headlines with an =OGENT_ID= property:

#+begin_src org
,** My Custom Review
:PROPERTIES:
:OGENT_ID: my-review
:END:
Review this code with special attention to:
- Our team's coding standards
- Integration with the legacy API
#+end_src

** Per-Project Customization

Set =ogent-project-prompts-file= in =.dir-locals.el= to load project-specific templates:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
((nil . ((ogent-project-prompts-file . "prompts.org"))))
#+end_src

Override existing templates with =ogent-prompt-overrides=:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
((nil . ((ogent-prompt-overrides
          . (("code-review" . (:content "Review with our team standards...")))))))
#+end_src

** Yasnippet Integration

Enable yasnippet integration for quick template insertion:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-hook 'org-mode-hook #'ogent-prompts-yasnippet-mode)
#+end_src

Then type =@code-review= and press TAB to expand the template.

#+title: ogent agent interface

Load ogent normally, then call local tools by name. These SDK workflows need
no provider login or inference. Paths resolve against =ogent-tools-project-root=
when set, otherwise the detected project/default directory.

* Read a file, then follow its pages

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(let ((page (ogent-agent-call "read" '(:file_path "README.org" :limit 40)))
      pages)
  (while (equal (plist-get page :status) "ok")
    (push (plist-get page :data) pages)
    (setq page (ogent-agent-next page)))
  (list :pages (vconcat (nreverse pages)) :terminal page))
#+end_src

=ogent-agent-next= follows the exact next position, including the column inside
a long line. It accepts a result plist or JSON string. A successful final page
becomes =done= on the next call. Check the terminal status before combining
pages: =snapshot_changed= means restart the original call. Continuations keep
absolute targets, so changing the current directory cannot redirect a page.

Read =data= contains =lines= with =number=, =column=, =text=, and =partial=,
plus =content=, =total_lines=, =snapshot=, and =ends_with_newline=. Columns count
characters from 1. The newline flag describes the original file; =content=
joins the returned line fragments and does not append that final newline.
Use positions to join partial lines rather than inserting newlines between
every page. Empty files succeed with zero lines.
Structured file paths must be Unicode; unsupported raw filename bytes return
=unsupported_output=, including one terminal error callback in asynchronous JSON calls.

* Discover and search in one batch

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(ogent-agent-batch
 '[(:tool "files" :args (:pattern "**/*.el" :path "lisp" :limit 5))
   (:tool "search" :args (:pattern "defun" :path "lisp"
                         :glob_filter "*.el" :context_lines 1 :limit 5))
   (:tool "read" :args (:file_path "README.org" :limit 20))])
#+end_src

The batch validates all calls before executing any and accepts up to 20 tools
whose declared effects are read-only. It uses the same result envelope as
individual calls, with =results=, =requested=, =completed=, and =stopped= under
=data=, and status =ok= or =partial=. Pass =t= as the third
argument to stop after the first unsuccessful call; the default continues.
Preflight failures return the ordinary error envelope and execute nothing.
Shell commands and writes need individual calls through approval.

=files= returns file objects with =path=, =size=, and =modified=, ordered by
absolute path. =**= matches zero or more directory levels. =search= returns
match objects with =path=, =line=, =text=, =context_before=, =context_after=,
and =truncated=. Both report totals and snapshot identities. No matches is
successful empty data. Search uses ripgrep when available or GNU grep with
xargs; the fallback uses extended regular expressions.

* Find the exact contract

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(ogent-agent-describe "read" 'json) ; One tool's arguments, aliases, and examples
(ogent-agent-capabilities 'json)    ; All live tool contracts and approval metadata
(ogent-agent-schema 'json)          ; JSON Schema for the result envelope
(ogent-agent-guide)                 ; Copyable local SDK handbook
#+end_src

Use =call_arguments= for =ogent-agent-call= and =ogent-agent-call-async=.
The legacy positional schema is =arguments=; named calls also accept result
pagination arguments such as =column= and search/glob =offset= and =limit=.
=async_sdk= declares terminal callback support; =legacy_streaming= describes
the separate older streaming API. The =async= field refers to the primary
legacy tool function, so inspect =async_sdk= for the public asynchronous SDK.

Built-in aliases include =read=/=cat=, =files=/=find=, =search=, =shell=/=run=,
=write=, and =edit=. Canonical names and underscore aliases such as =read_file=
also work. Exact registered names win over aliases. Typos suggest corrections
and execute nothing. Discovery reads metadata without constructing tools or
contacting providers. An empty =tools= array means no specs are installed;
=(ogent-tools-install-defaults)= explicitly adds the built-in specs.

* Handle outcomes without parsing prose

=ogent-agent-call= returns =contract_version= ="1"=, =tool=, =status=, =data=,
=error=, and =next=. Pass ='json= as the final argument to serialize the same
result. Native collections are vectors; false and null use =:json-false= and
=:json-null=. Compare native result booleans with =t= rather than treating every
non-nil value as true. JSON uses ordinary arrays, booleans, and null.

| Status            | Next step                                              |
|-------------------+--------------------------------------------------------|
| ok                | Use data; follow next pages if present                  |
| done              | Pagination completed                                   |
| error             | Read error.code, message, and recovery                  |
| approval_required | Continue through normal user approval/review            |
| denied            | Respect the decision; ask the user to review the policy |
| proposed          | An edit awaits review; it has not been applied          |

Errors identify =unknown_tool=, =invalid_arguments=, =snapshot_changed=,
=async_required=, =unsafe_batch=, =dependency_missing=, =process_start_failed=,
=unsupported_output=, =search_failed=, =command_failed=, =timeout=, or
=cancelled= as applicable. Extension/execution failures can use
=execution_failed= or =unavailable=. Follow =recovery= rather than guessing
from a human log. Arguments reject missing required fields, unknown or duplicate
keys, wrong standard types, and invalid enums before approval or execution.
Native boolean input accepts =nil= or =:json-false=. MCP specs using JSON
booleans distinguish explicit =:json-false= from an omitted optional =nil=.

* Keep work bounded and cancellable

| Tool   | Position convention | Default page / bound                         |
|--------+---------------------+----------------------------------------------|
| read   | Line/column from 1  | Lesser of 200 and ogent-tools-max-file-lines  |
| files  | Offset from 0       | 100 files; at most 200 per page               |
| search | Offset from 0       | 200 matches; at most 20 context lines         |
| shell  | Positive seconds    | ogent-tools-shell-timeout, initially 120      |

=ogent-tools-max-output-chars= defaults to 30,000 characters for read content,
combined shell stdout/stderr, and retained search match/context text. Metadata
and the JSON envelope are outside that text budget. Read pages retain an exact
continuation through long lines. Search retains match locations even
when text/context is shortened; inspect =truncated= and read the matching file
for complete text. Search uses =ogent-tools-grep-timeout=, initially 30 seconds,
and rejects oversized wire records explicitly rather than claiming complete
results. Read snapshots identify decoded content, glob snapshots identify file
metadata, and search snapshots identify the observed match/context records.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(ogent-agent-call-async
 "search" '(:pattern "defun" :path "lisp" :limit 5)
 (lambda (result) (message "Search finished: %s" (plist-get result :status))))
#+end_src

The callback receives exactly one terminal envelope. The call returns a process
for asynchronous work or =nil= when it finishes immediately. Cancel a returned
process with =ogent-tool-process-cancel=. Legacy streaming callbacks and
=ogent-tools-stream-callback= have their own event shapes; they do not use this
one-result callback contract.

Structured read results require Unicode filenames and supported text encoding.
Unsupported raw bytes return =unsupported_output=; JSON serialization failures
from extension values also deliver a typed error, including async callbacks.

Shell =data= separates =stdout=, =stderr=, =exit_code=, =signal=, =timed_out=,
=cancelled=, and =truncated=. Nonzero exits, timeouts, and cancellation return
an error while retaining available output. =encoding_loss= marks UTF-8
replacement; =drain_incomplete= means some pipe output could not be collected
within the drain deadline and also marks the shell result truncated. Search
reports encoding loss when present and fails if it cannot fully drain its
output. Search failures do not claim a complete match page.

* Preserve approval and existing integrations

Public calls use the shared approval, edit review, and ledger owners. They
never grant approval or prompt from the programmatic SDK. Read-only built-ins
need no confirmation by default; writes and shell calls require a decision
unless existing policy already permits them. An edit's =old_string= must be
nonempty and unique unless =replace_all= is explicitly true. A failed review
acceptance remains available for retry or rejection.

Existing =ogent-tool--*= primitives default to their text results. Explicit
=plist= or =json= format arguments select structured data for read/search/shell
primitives; these are low-level calls, so use =ogent-agent-call= for policy and
ledger enforcement. The public agent SDK returns structured envelopes without
changing the text format chosen by existing integrations.

Opt normal registered model-facing calls into the same JSON envelopes:

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(setq ogent-tools-result-format 'json)
(ogent-register-tools)
#+end_src

JSON mode exposes the result pagination arguments in gptel's tool schema and
keeps calls in the shared approval, review, and ledger flow. Registration
regenerates tool objects when the format changes. Switch before assembling the
next request's tool list; objects already held by a caller retain their captured
format. Set the option back to =text= and re-register to restore legacy results.
This changes local tool formatting and registration; it does not log into a
provider or run inference.

* Verify and diagnose locally

=(ogent-agent-triage 'json)= combines discovery, local doctor results, and next
actions. It excludes opt-in network checks. =(ogent-doctor-batch nil 'json)=
returns structured health with exit 0 for ok/info, 1 for warnings, and 2 for
errors. Local diagnostics may inspect credential metadata but do not log in
or run inference.

=make test format=json= and =make lint format=json= run the actual build helper
with one versioned JSON report on stdout and diagnostics on stderr. Inspect
tasks, real command exits, compiler locations, and ERT counts. Discover the
build contract with =./makem.sh --capabilities --json=; see
[[file:build-reporting.org][build reporting]] for the exit dictionary.

=make test-isolation= checks that tests leave real stores unchanged.
=OGENT_ELPA_DIR=/path/to/elpa make offline-test= exercises actual dependencies
with loopback and fixture processes; =OGENT_GPTEL_DIR= optionally selects a
supported gptel checkout. =EMACS=PATH= selects the build executable, and
=make help= lists the available commands.
